criteria: C4 known-invalid patterns under the Three-Law hierarchy (CLAUDE.md). Owner findings triaged per Law 3: obvious-harm misconfig / malicious-owner = INVALID; non-obvious footgun unknowingly enabling an exploit or breaking a story = VALID operational hazard.

checks.note: Concrete root cause: unwrapped phUSD.mint at PhlimboV3._claimRewards:863, asymmetric with the try+bank-wrapped stable (:876) and promo (:902) legs.

Law-3 triage: trigger is the GLOBAL phUSD kill-switch (revokeAllMintPrivileges/setMinter false) an operator pulls to contain an UNRELATED minter incident. The V3 principal freeze is a non-obvious cross-contract side effect a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised by. Not owner malice, not obvious-harm misconfig. Passes the surprise test -> footgun, in scope.

validityChecks.notes: VALID Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun. Owner is exercising a legitimate ecosystem-wide safety action, not an obviously-destructive misconfig (compare price=0 / point-to-malicious-token). The freeze reaches into an unrelated staking contract's principal path via an asymmetric un-wrapped mint leg the operator has no reason to anticipate. Recoverable + privileged-trigger correctly caps severity at Low (does NOT inherit Medium parent V3-M-05, whose trigger was UNprivileged USDC-blocklist). Keep in scope with safe-config guidance.
validityChecks.recommendation: Retain as Low footgun with INCOMPLETE-FIX flag on V3-M-05. Do not suppress.

checks.note: Concrete structural root cause: MigratorV2V3 has no forwarder that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimableStable/Promo for itself -> its own PhlimboV3-side bank is unreachable via the migrator.
No owner malice; owner is the RECOVERY actor (emergencyTransfer), not the cause.

The trigger requires a blocklisting token (e.g. USDC) to blocklist the migrator's OWN address mid-straggler-pass. Blocklist tokens are in scope for this project (per phlimbo-ea prior runs USDC blocklist was the accepted vector for V3-M-05), so this is NOT the weird-ERC20 known-invalid. But the impact is a design gap (missing self-pull forwarder), not the token behavior itself.

validityChecks.notes: VALID but genuinely low/informational. Root cause is a first-party design gap (missing forwarder), owner-recoverable, no theft, no permanent loss, exotic self-blocklist precondition. Not a known-invalid: the value stranding is intrinsic to MigratorV2V3's own missing self-pull, with the blocklist only as the entry precondition. Blocklist tokens are established as in-scope for this project.
validityChecks.recommendation: Retain as Low/informational design footgun. Confirm it does not duplicate V3-L-08 / V3-F-01 / V3-Q-01 (classifier asserts distinct banks/root-causes).

concerns: DEDUP-10-002 rests on a blocklist-token precondition; valid only because blocklist tokens are already accepted in scope for phlimbo-ea and the root cause is a first-party design gap, not the token weirdness.
